business_scope.primary_industry_name: Commercial Mail Receiving Agency (CMRA) and Digital Scanning

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Colombia (National Unified Jurisdiction, no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (unitary national codified legal system with modern commercial code and constitutional review)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Colombia–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 2012)
Colombia–European Union Free Trade Agreement (in force 2013)
Colombia–United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement (in force 2021)
Colombia–Japan Agreement for the Liberalization, Promotion and Protection of Investment (in force 2015)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 526 de 1999 and Decreto 830 de 2021 (UIAF AML/CFT regime, obliged-entity CDD duties); Ley 1121 de 2006 (terrorism-financing offenses); Estatuto Tributario articles 631-5 and 631-6 as amended by Ley 2010 de 2019 and Decreto 2181 de 2021 (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales - RUB); DIAN Resolución 164 de 2021 (RUB filing protocols); Circular Básica Jurídica (Superintendencia Financiera) as incorporated by reference for supervised sectors. The statutory UBO definition captures any individual directly or indirectly owning 10% or more of capital or voting rights, or exercising de facto control; enhanced CDD is independently triggered at ownership levels of 25% or more under general AML standards.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Certificate of Existence of the non-resident corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry of the shareholder's country of origin (e.g., Companies House U.K., Secretary of State U.S.A.)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Colombia is a contracting party since 2001); consular legalization required only for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Solvency Certificate of the non-resident corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (Poder General) appointing the incorporator and legal representative of the S.A.S.
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin, or Colombian Notaría if executed locally
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for foreign notarized execution; direct notarization if executed before a Colombian notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO sworn affidavit (Declaración Jurada de Beneficiario Final) with certified passport copies of all beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin or Colombian Notaría; sworn translator (traductor oficial) for the Spanish version
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or notarization accepted; official Spanish translation required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory continuous screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, attorneys-in-fact and material counterparties against: (i) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) and 50% Ownership Rule lists; (ii) UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (iii) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (iv) Colombian UIAF and Consejo de Seguridad Nacional designations, including the locally incorporated OFAC-derived 'Lista de Clinton' alert list; and (v) Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) databases covering domestic, foreign and international-organization PEPs as defined by Decreto 830 de 2021. Screening is performed before onboarding and refreshed continuously; results are archived in the AML compliance file for five (5) years; any sanctioned or unverified UBO triggers immediate refusal of incorporation services and, where applicable, a Suspicious Transaction Report to the UIAF.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial (RUE) via the local Cámara de Comercio of the intended domicile (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá; official online portals: www.rue.com.co and www.ccb.org.co)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be expressed in Spanish or in a generally accepted Latin-alphabet form; any foreign expression must be transliterated into Latin script and must not misrepresent the legal form; the name of an S.A.S. must end with the token 'S.A.S.' or the full denomination 'Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada'. The name must be distinctive, must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company or trademark, and must comply with Decree 1074 de 2015 (Merchant Registry and Company Name provisions).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco / Bancario (requires prior authorization of the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia)
Seguros / Aseguradora (requires prior authorization of the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia)
Financiera / Fiduciaria / Leasing / Bolsa de Valores (requires prior authorization of the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia)
Cooperativa (requires prior authorization of the Superintendencia de la Economía Solidaria)
Colombia / Colombiano / Nacional (requires prior ministerial or competent authority approval)
Ministerio / Gobernación / Alcaldía / Presidencia (official-government tokens prohibited)
Droguería / Farmacia (requires prior INVIMA sanitary authorization)
Mining / Petróleo / Minerales (may require sector authority clearance under certain regimes)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a 'recurso de reposición' with the competent Cámara de Comercio within five (5) business days of notification; if denied, a 'recurso de apelación' may be submitted to the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) within the same five-day window after the revisory decision. Alternatively, the applicant may immediately request a new name reservation at no additional charge. The rejection notice, appeal briefs and final decision must be archived in the incorporation file as evidence of name-clearance due diligence.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible with conditions for the S.A.S. operating a CMRA/virtual-office mail-scanning business: the registered office (domicilio social) must be a real physical address in Colombia at which legal notices and official correspondence can be served; a post-office box alone is not acceptable. Because the CMRA activity itself constitutes the company's commercial substance, the address must be duly habilitated under Ley 1369 de 2009 and MinTIC postal-services regulations, and must be reflected in the RUE registry and in all corporate and tax filings.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-elevated risk: estimated 40% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 12 months of operation. The Cámara de Comercio, Superintendencia de Sociedades, MinTIC and tax/AML authorities may verify the registered office, mail-handling records and UBO documentation; the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML tier assigned to CMRA activities increases the likelihood of supervisory visits.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate name reservation and RUES preliminary distinctiveness search
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (via RUE portal)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff (approximately COP 10,000–20,000 per reservation request)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille / consular legalization of four (4) origin-country corporate documents (certificate of incorporation, good standing, power of attorney, UBO affidavit)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authority in the country of origin (e.g., Secretary of State, FCDO, Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market fee (approximately USD 30 per document; consular legalization in non-Hague jurisdictions is higher)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation into Spanish of apostilled corporate documents and power of attorney (traductor oficial)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Official translator (traductor oficial) registered with the Ministerio de Justicia y del Derecho
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate per source page (approximately USD 25–35 per page)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of S.A.S. constituent document, UBO sworn affidavits and acknowledgment of power of attorney before Colombian Notaría
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial fee schedule regulated by the Superintendencia de Notariado y Registro

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Merchant registration (Matrícula Mercantil) and RUE enrollment of the S.A.S.
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for the minimum-asset brackets (approximately COP 300,000–500,000)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NIT / RUT tax registration before DIAN
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory fee; mandatory registration processed electronically

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RUB (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales) filing and annual confirmation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory fee; mandatory annual filing under Resolución 164 de 2021

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: External corporate counsel fees: drafting of S.A.S. bylaws, pre-incorporation due diligence, AML/UBO filings and ministerial clearance support

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML compliance data vendor engaged through local counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (annual subscription for one entity)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 1258 of 2008 (Ley 1258 de 2008) on Sociedades por Acciones Simplificadas, especially Articles 1, 4, 5, 10, 17-24 and 32-37, harmonized with Articles 98 et seq. of the Colombian Code of Commerce (Código de Comercio) and Decree 1074 of 2015 (Decreto Único Reglamentario del Sector Comercio).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Chamber of Commerce of the registered domicile, operating through the Single Business and Social Registry (Registro Único Empresarial y Social - RUES), with entity law oversight by the Superintendencia de Sociedades (Bogotá, Colombia).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Commercial Registry registration (Matrícula Mercantil) of the private incorporation document (Documento Privado de Constitución) filed through the RUES portal, followed by issuance of the Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation (Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal) and tax identification in the DIAN RUT.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital. The S.A.S. may be incorporated with one share subscribed and fully paid at a nominal value (e.g. COP 1); deferred payment of future services may extend up to two years. No escrow account is required under Law 1258/2008 for cash subscriptions; in-kind capital contributions require attachment of the transfer instrument to the deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The sole shareholder, as legitimate competent corporate body, adopts this First Board Resolution for the Colombian S.A.S.: (1) subscription and full payment of the authorized capital according to Article 2 of the by-laws; (2) adoption of the registered office at the domicile stated in the certificate of incorporation; (3) appointment of the legal representative, principal and alternate, with corporate powers under Law 1258/2008; (4) ratification of the company's object encompassing commercial mail receiving agency and digital scanning, and authorization to execute administrative filings, open bank accounts, and complete the RUT registration before the DIAN; (5) recording of minutes in the corporate books. Approved unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name reservation and legal form check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chamber of Commerce of the domicile via the Single Business Registry portal (www.rues.org.co)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to three corporate-name options in the RUES name-search module, choosing the legal form S.A.S. and CIIU code 8299. Verify that no existing company has an identical or phonetically similar name, then reserve the selected name for 30 days.
required_dossiers: Incorporator's ID or tax number (NIT)
Three proposed corporate names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity with an existing entity, resubmit with modified names in the same RUES session or request an expedited administrative review by the Chamber of Commerce.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Constituent shareholders and legal counsel; notarization optional under Law 1258/2008
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the by-laws containing the corporate name, domicile, corporate purpose covering ISIC 8299 virtual office and mail scanning, capital subscription and payment terms, governance bodies, legal representative powers, quorum rules, and dissolution causes. The document must be signed by all shareholders and the appointed legal representative accepting his or her position.
required_dossiers: Final draft of by-laws
Signed acceptance letters of the legal representative and officers
Certified IDs or passports of the shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a shareholder challenges any clause, amend the by-laws by unanimous private agreement before registration or formalize a reform act (reforma) for submission with the registry application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial registry registration and provisional NIT issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chamber of Commerce of the registered domicile with DIAN integration via RUES
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed private incorporation document through RUES, pay the commercial registry tariff, and obtain the provisional NIT automatically generated by the Chamber. After review, the Chamber issues the Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation simultaneously with the Mercantile Registry certificate.
required_dossiers: Executed private incorporation document
Pre-RUT information and NIT data of shareholders
Receipt of the registration fee
Proof of registered office, lease or virtual-office service agreement covering mail scanning
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber issues an official query (requerimiento), respond within 10 business days with corrected clauses or request a 30-day extension; after approval, any residual defect may be cured by filing an amendment in the same registry file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: DIAN RUT finalization, electronic signature, and e-invoicing activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN - Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales via the MUISCA portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the provisional NIT to finalize the RUT registration in MUISCA, confirming the CIIU 8299 code, municipal ICA responsibility, VAT status, and applicable national taxes. Download the digital signature certificate and activate electronic invoicing through the DIAN software or an authorized software provider.
required_dossiers: Provisional NIT certificate
Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation
Original ID of the legal representative
Corporate email and mobile phone
By-laws summary for the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUT is placed in an incorrect tax status, file an immediate actualización del RUT through the MUISCA portal; if DIAN sends a formal requerimiento, answer with documentary evidence within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of corporate bank account and payment rail enablement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Selected Colombian commercial bank (e.g., Bancolombia, Davivienda, Banco de Bogotá) with AML compliance officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the incorporation package to the SMEs segment to open a corporate current account. Submit the board resolution appointing signatories and complete enhanced due diligence required for the CMRA/mail-scanning activity classified as medium-risk. After opening, enable national and international transfers, Stripe Recurring settlements, and credit-card acquiring integration.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation issued not more than 30 days earlier
RUT of the company
By-laws
Board resolution appointing bank signatories
Passports, IDs and utility bills of legal representatives and ultimate beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank's compliance team requests additional documentation, provide the enhanced KYC questionnaire and sworn source-of-funds declaration. If the account opening is rejected, apply to another bank or escalate to the bank's transactional risk committee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal commercial operation license and ICA tax registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía Mayor / Secretaría de Hacienda for the municipal Industry and Commerce Tax (ICA) and the local urban zoning authority (Curaduría Urbana)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the covered business for ICA under CIIU 8299. Submit the registered-office lease or ownership proof and certify that the virtual office and mail-scanning activity is a professional service without manufacturing equipment. Obtain the municipal operating license (Registro de Actividad Comercial) and verify the zoning certificate allows commercial or office use.
required_dossiers: RUT
Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation
Lease or ownership certificate of the registered address
Zoning certificate or land-use certificate (Certificado de Uso de Suelo)
ICA registration form through the municipal integrated portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the zoning certificate rejects the commercial use, apply for a variance or an exception for knowledge-based service companies, or relocate the registered office to a property with a compatible urban use.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate governance book setup and beneficial ownership filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Superintendencia de Sociedades (SIRI / Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales - RUBF) and the Chamber of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create the shareholders registry, corporate minutes book, and books required under comercial law. File the beneficial ownership report through the SIRI module if any shareholder holds 5% or more of capital or control rights, and inscribe the foreign investment details with the Chamber of Commerce for statistical and tax purposes.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation
Initial balance sheet or asset statement
List of shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners
Copy of first board resolution
RUT
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the beneficial-ownership information is inconsistent, file a corrective statement with the Superintendencia de Sociedades within 15 days and update the Chamber of Commerce registry accordingly.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alcaldía Mayor of the domicile and Curaduría Urbana for commercial-use zoning; Comisión de Regulación de Comunicaciones (CRC) and MinTIC if the CMRA service is characterized as an added-value mailbox management activity requiring postal accounting registration.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Matrícula Mercantil with CIIU 8299, Local Business Operating License (Registro de Actividad Comercial) and Municipal ICA Certificate (Certificado de Industria y Comercio).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Corporación Autónoma Regional (CAR) or Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) depending on the municipal circumscription; local environmental authorities for the registered office.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category IV (no full Environmental Impact Assessment required for virtual office and mail-scanning services under Decree 1076 of 2015); only an environmental execution report is required if physical premises exceeds 20 workers or generates special waste.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or combustion emissions generated by the core activity. Domestic wastewater must comply with Resolution 0631 of 2015, and all electronic waste (scanners, computers, printers) must be delivered to authorized RAEE collectors under Resolution 1512 of 2010, with a waste management record.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification from the Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos, structural load and evacuation-route inspection for commercial premises above 50 m² by the local emergency management agency (IDIGER in Bogotá), and workplace clearance under the SG-SST requirements of Decreto 1072 of 2015 and Resolution 0312 of 2019.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN); portal: www.dian.gov.co; transactional platform: MUISCA (Modelo Único de Ingresos, Servicio y Control Automatizado).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned S.A.S. is formed by filing a private incorporation document or public deed with the Chamber of Commerce in the relevant jurisdiction. Once the Chamber registers the company, DIAN issues the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria). The legal representative must complete and validate the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) in MUISCA, record ISIC 8299 as the principal economic activity, mark the company as a VAT-responsible electronic-invoicing taxpayer, and obtain DIAN web-services credentials and a digital certificate. Non-resident shareholders may lawfully own the S.A.S.; the S.A.S. is itself the taxpayer for income tax, VAT, and ancillary taxes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia does not provide a check-the-box election or any elective hybrid-mismatch classification. An S.A.S. is always taxed as a separate Colombian-resident entity. The principal statutory election is the Régimen Simple de Tributación (RST), an optional integrated tax regime for eligible small and medium service enterprises; the election is made through the RUT and, once in force, replaces income tax, VAT, and municipal industry-and-commerce tax with a consolidated charge subject to annual revenue limits and DIAN oversight.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: COP 0 for corporate taxpayers. An S.A.S. performing habitual taxable activities must be registered in the RUT as a VAT responsible person before beginning operations; no minimum turnover exemption exists for companies. Under the individual non-responsibility rule, a natural person may avoid VAT responsibility only if prior-year taxable gross income did not exceed 3,500 UVT (approx. COP 164.7 million for 2024); this is not available to an S.A.S.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory. Every VAT-responsible S.A.S. must issue electronic sales invoices (factura electrónica de venta – FEV) using DIAN-authorized software or DIAN web services. Each FEV must include the CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica) and a QR code, and must be transmitted to DIAN electronically; DIAN responds with an acceptance or rejection online on the MUISCA platform when the invoice is submitted. Invoices, credit notes, debit notes and supporting export documents must be stored in the DIAN-designated XML format with sequential numbers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from Colombian customs territory are IVA-exempt at 0% and the exporter may reclaim VAT borne on inputs. Services, including ISIC 8299 virtual-office mail scanning and digital document services, qualify for the 0% export rate when the beneficiary is a non-resident without a Colombian permanent establishment, the economic use and benefit of the service occurs outside Colombia, the service is not an activity supplied for consumption in Colombia, and the exporter channels the fee through the Colombian foreign-exchange market. The exporter must maintain evidence of the residence status of the foreign client and the actual performance of the service abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Goods exports: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) filed in MUISCA/SIIS and the DIAN-approved export document showing departure from Colombian customs territory.
Transport document: Bill of Lading, House Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing dispatch to the foreign consignee.
Commercial invoice and, for service exports, the signed service contract describing the ISIC 8299 virtual-office or mail-scanning services and the non-resident beneficiary.
Inward Remittance Certificate (certificado de negociación de divisas) issued by an authorized bank evidencing settlement of the export proceeds through the Colombian FX market.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN cross-validates export refunds against customs declarations, service contracts, beneficiary residency documentation, electronic invoices, and FX records. Any zero-rating claimed without a genuine export, without receipt and 180-day repatriation of foreign currency, or using fraudulent documentation is retroactively disallowed; DIAN will assess full IVA at 19% plus default interest, impose the Article 647 E.T. inaccuracy penalty equal to 100% of the overstated refund, and may order administrative suspension or closure measures. Fraudulent refund schemes may also be referred for criminal tax fraud prosecution.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso (COP) operates under a managed free float with a two-tier convertibility framework. Current-account transactions such as the export and import of services, royalty payments, and operating remittances are freely convertible when channelled through the organised foreign exchange market, which is composed of commercial banks and foreign exchange intermediaries supervised by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia and regulated by Banco de la República. Capital-account operations, including foreign direct investment in a Colombian S.A.S., must be recorded through an exchange declaration (Formulario 11) and registered on the Banco de la República international investment register; registration is a condition precedent for the future outflow of dividends, capital reductions, or share redemptions. There are no express quantitative caps on profit remittances of a compliant foreign investor, but the remittance is subject to standard Colombian dividend withholding taxation and the investor must maintain an updated registration of the investment. For an ISIC 8299 virtual office and mail scanning enterprise, the main practical hurdle is procedural: all inbound equity and outbound operational settlements must be traceable through the regulated banking circuit so that the central bank's exchange declaration and the tax administration's NIT records remain consistent.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Colombian foreign exchange regime, exporters of services, including mail scanning and virtual office services classified under ISIC 8299, must collect their export proceeds within twelve months counted from the issuance of the corresponding export invoice or from the filing of the export declaration with the bank (Formulario 14), whichever is applicable. There is no mandatory conversion ratio into COP; the exporter may lawfully retain the proceeds in a foreign currency account abroad, provided that any such account is reported to Banco de la República as a cuenta de compensación and that periodic declarations are filed. If the exporter elects to convert the proceeds, the conversion must be executed through the formal foreign exchange market at a bank, and the bank will record the operation. Where payment is received in domestic currency from an international card settling house such as Stripe, the service export must still be reported through Formulario 14, and the company must retain the merchant settlement statements, card network reports, and underlying client invoices as evidence of the export transaction. Failure to comply with the twelve-month repatriation or collection term, or failure to file the corresponding exchange declaration, may trigger graduated fines and the potential exclusion of the operation from the tax benefit of service exports.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (cuenta para aportes de capital) and Operational Account (cuenta corriente COP, USD and foreign currency sub-accounts)
Operational Account (cuenta corriente COP) with international wire desk and USD mirror account
Operational Account (cuenta corriente) with multi-divisa treasury facilities and merchant settlement support
Operational Account (cuenta corriente COP) and captive foreign currency current account
Operational Account with trade finance and FX hedging desk
Institutional Corporate Operational Account with international cash management and custody

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for collections-only auxiliary use, Low for use as a primary treasury account. An offshore electronic money institution (EMI) such as Wise, Revolut Business, or Airwallex is not a supervised foreign exchange intermediary in Colombia and cannot open an onshore COP account in the name of the S.A.S. Holdings in such an EMI are characterised as funds maintained abroad and therefore fall within the cuenta de compensación reporting regime if the account belongs to a Colombian tax resident entity. Receipts from international card networks through Stripe, when settled directly to a Colombian bank account, remain the preferred legal and operational rail for the recurring subscription model. The S.A.S. may use an EMI for small-disbursement vendor payments outside Colombia, but all proceeds must be reconciled with Formulario 14 filings, and the core operating liquidity must sit in a tier-1 local bank to preserve exchange-control compliance and future dividend remittance capacity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no universal statutory requirement that every director of a Colombian S.A.S. appear physically at the bank branch; however, the legal representative or a person with a notarised and apostilled power of attorney must satisfy the bank's Sanction and AML/CFT identity verification programme. In practice, tier-1 banks require at least one authorised signatory to complete a biometric verification and a recorded interview, and this step generally occurs physically in Colombia for the opening of a corporate account. For foreign resident directors, banks will normally accept a remote video interview with passport biometric verification only if the company also appoints a domiciled agent in Colombia for judicial and administrative notifications, and if the corporate documentation is legalised and apostilled. Some banks, particularly Bancolombia and BBVA, allow non-resident legal representatives to sign through a Colombian-appointed attorney. The absence of a local bank interview is a material risk, and the onboarding strategy should therefore include a Colombian-based compliance representative or a visit by the foreign legal representative to sign the account opening minutes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered office and operating address are a virtual office or commercial mail receiving facility, which raises the bank's suspicion of shell-company formation or unregulated mail-forwarding activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a verified lease agreement with the virtual office operator, current Cámara de Comercio registry certificate showing the operational address and statutory address, geolocated photographs or video of the receiving and scanning equipment, the postal-service activity authorisation or registration with the Ministry of ICT (Ventanilla Única de Servicios Postales) if the operation entails regulated mail receipt, a summary of the mail scanning workflow, and a list of representative commercial clients evidencing the substantive business model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: One hundred percent ownership by non-resident shareholders, especially if the shareholder jurisdiction is a high-risk or offshore financial centre, triggers enhanced due diligence on the ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver notarised and apostilled corporate documents of the foreign holding company, a full UBO identification form covering every natural person with twenty-five percent or more ownership, source-of-wealth statements supported by foreign tax returns or bank references, criminal record certificates from the country of residence, and an executed local agent power of attorney for service of process in Colombia.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High expected volumes of micro-credit-card transactions from international subscription clients, potentially interpreted by the bank as card mule activity or unverified layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the Stripe merchant agreement and historical settlement statements, PCI-DSS Level 1 attestation of compliance, chargeback and dispute ratios below one percent, the public price list of the virtual office and mail scanning services, sample client contracts, and a projection of expected monthly transaction volumes segregated by acquiring channel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The company has received foreign capital contributions without having filed the Banco de la República foreign investment registration, creating a legal impediment to the bank account mandate and future dividend outflows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the draft or stamped exchange declaration Formulario 11 for the initial capital contribution, evidence of the wire remittance from the shareholder such as the MT103 token, the corporate minutes approving the capital increase, a compliance undertaking committing the company to register the investment within the twelve-month legal term, and subsequent proof of registration with Banco de la República once issued.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant routing protocol for inbound foreign equity for the Colombian S.A.S. requires the foreign shareholder to send a SWIFT MT103 transfer from its own corporate bank account to the S.A.S. bank account held in Colombia, naming the S.A.S. NIT in the beneficiary field and stating in the payment narrative the purpose as aporte de capital, inversion directa de no residentes en Colombia. The receiving tier-1 bank, for example Bancolombia S.A. with SWIFT BIC COLCCOBM, records the operation and produces the exchange declaration Formulario 11 under the direct investment concept codes contained in Circular Reglamentaria DCIN-83, Annex 1. If the S.A.S. is capitalised in COP, the bank converts the foreign currency at the market exchange rate and the exchange declaration evidences the capital contribution. If the contribution is maintained in a foreign currency account, the account must be flagged for foreign investment registration purposes. The company then files the formal international investment registration with Banco de la República within twelve months of the wire, and the bank remains the channel for the registration because it has the operative exchange declaration. Payments received through online EMI platforms, cryptocurrency, or third-party card processors are not accepted as valid evidence for the foreign direct investment registration and must not be used for capital injections. After registration, the S.A.S. may lawfully remit dividends, distributions, and the proceeds of capital reductions to the foreign shareholder subject to Colombian tax withholding.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade and operating purposes, including software licensing, cloud hosting, overseas subcontractors, and international marketing services, should be executed through the SWIFT MT103 clearing rail via the company's local bank. The bank files the corresponding exchange declaration Formulario 14 under the service import concept code of Circular DCIN-83 Annex 1. Each payment must be supported by a commercial invoice issued to the S.A.S., a signed service agreement, and when the payment is made prior to delivery, the advance payment clause of the agreement. Payment against a commercial letter of credit is not typical for service disbursements under ISIC 8299, but a standby letter of credit may be used as a performance or rent guarantee for the premises of the virtual office. For recurring small-value payments to foreign vendors, the company may aggregate them into a monthly treasury run to minimise bank fees and facilitate reconciliation. Every payment instruction must repeat the invoice number in the remittance information field, and the company must retain the bank's foreign exchange liquidation and the corresponding MT103 as the audit trail for the DIAN and Banco de la República. The bank's designated corporate treasury portal should be used exclusively; outgoing payments from an offshore EMI remain reportable and should be avoided where possible.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/COP foreign exchange forward contracts (OTC) entered into with a Colombian credit entity authorised to operate the foreign exchange market.
Non-deliverable USD/COP forwards (NDFs) with an onshore bank or an offshore counterparty where the reference rate is the Colombian Central Bank's representative market rate (TRM).
USD/COP cross-currency swaps allowing the company to swap fixed or floating USD receipts into COP liabilities and manage tenor risk on subscription cash flows.
Plain-vanilla USD/COP call and put options and zero-cost collar or corridor structures executed through a local brokerage or bank treasury desk.
Listed USD/COP futures and unified TRM settlement contracts traded on the Colombian Stock Exchange or through its authorised clearing houses for corporate hedging positions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Registry Annual Renewal (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil) and deposit of approved Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Chamber of Commerce (Cámara de Comercio) of the company's domicile; supervised by Superintendencia de Sociedades
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 of each year (calendar year end: December 31)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers a 5% surcharge on the registry fee (C.Com. Art. 35); non-renewal for two consecutive years may result in administrative strike-off/cancellation of the registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: April 14–April 30 of each year, staggered by last two digits of the NIT (per DIAN annual resolution)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Extemporaneity fine of 5% of tax due per month (or fraction) of delay, capped at 100% of tax; if no tax due, 1% of gross income (max 10,000 UVT); default interest under ET Art. 634; failure to file may trigger DIAN assessment (ET Art. 641, 714).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between mid-February and late March (approx. 20 business days), staggered by NIT last two digits
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: General information sanction under ET Art. 651: up to 5% of the underlying values or up to 15,000 UVT for failure to file, incorrect, or inexact data.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal Industry and Commerce Tax Annual Return (Declaración Anual del Impuesto de Industria y Comercio)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipal treasury (e.g., Secretaría Distrital de Hacienda, Bogotá D.C.)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in April (typically April 22–30 for Bogotá), staggered by NIT; deadline may vary by municipality
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Municipal late-filing fine of 5% of the tax per month (or fraction) of delay, capped at 100%; default interest at municipal rate; repeated non-filing enables assessed liquidation and an administrative suspension of the business establishment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Registry Confirmation (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the corporate income tax return deadline (approx. early June); also within 30 business days after any share transfer or ownership/control change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or update the RUB is penalized under ET Art. 651 (up to 15,000 UVT); the registration is a prerequisite for government contracts and tax procedures; no fee for filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders' General Meeting: approval of financial statements and distribution of profits (or sole shareholder written resolution)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate minutes book; summary minutes filed with the Chamber of Commerce together with financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end, i.e., by March 31 of each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: There is no administrative fine for holding a late meeting, but accounts remain unobtained and undistributable; the Chamber may require a certification of the meeting as part of the annual renewal if dividends are to be withdrawn, and third-party reliance on approved accounts is impaired.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory Revisor Fiscal (statutory statutory auditor) for a S.A.S. when total assets exceed 3,000 minimum monthly legal salaries (SMMLV) (= COP 4,270,500,000 ≈ USD 1,050,000 for FY2025) OR gross income exceeds 3,000 SMMLV OR the company has more than 30 employees (Law 1258/2008, Art. 23; C.Com. Art. 203). Entities classified in Grupo 1 under Decree 2420/2015 (assets > 30,000 SMMLV or > 200 employees) must adopt full IFRS and mandatory independent audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian GAAP for Grupo 2 (SMEs): NIIF para las Pymes (IFRS for SMEs), adopted by Decree 2420/2015 (amended by Decrees 2496/2015, 2131/2016, 2170/2017 and 2483/2018); Grupo 1 applies full IFRS as issued by IASB. Financial statements are presented in Colombian pesos (COP) on an accrual basis with a December 31 year-end.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: DIAN Resolution 164/2021 requires each legal entity to file an annual update of the RUB (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales) within 30 business days of the deadline for the annual income tax return, and within 30 business days of any change in direct or indirect ownership of 5% or more or any variation in control. The filing is submitted electronically via the MUISCA portal, after(*), no registration fee. The shareholder register (Libro de Registro de Accionistas) must record each share transfer, and the RUB must be updated to reflect the new ultimate beneficiary; for non-resident shareholders, the transfer must also be registered with the Banco de la República under the foreign direct investment regime.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Shareholders (Libro de Registro de Accionistas)
Register of Directors (Libro de Actas de la Junta Directiva and appointment register)
Minutes Book of the General Shareholders' Meeting (Libro de Actas de la Asamblea)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,200-4,500 per year when Revisor Fiscal / statutory audit threshold is triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 35% (general rate for FY2025, Art. 240 of the Colombian Tax Statute as amended by Law 2277/2022)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No sectoral CIT reduction applies to CMRA/mail-scanning services. Relevant statutory benefits: (i) 25% tax credit for qualifying R&D investments (Art. 256-1 E.T.); (ii) enhanced deductions for hiring unemployed youth, individuals with disabilities, and certain SME payroll (Art. 108-2, 271 E.T.); (iii) elimination of ICU subsidies for new 'orange economy' ventures (Art. 235-2 numeral 8 E.T.). For a virtual-office SAS, the practical effective rate is 35% absent qualifying incentives.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no year cap); annual offset of tax losses is restricted to 25% of taxable income for losses generated in 2017–2021, 30% for losses generated 2022–2024, rising to 35%/40%/50% for later years (Art. 147 E.T.).
